docTitle: Should you still learn to code in 2026? 4 skills that matter now

slides.title: Should you learn to code if only *4.5%* of US dev job posts are entry level?
slides.sub: I'm a software developer. This is what I'd tell a beginner in 2026.

slides.title: Software had the smallest entry-level share

shot.quote: ranging from *91.3%* in personal care & home health to *4.5%* in software development in Q1 2026

slides.title: Developer job posts went up. {*71%* of the new ones were senior.}

shot.quote: *71%* of the increase in software development job postings between May 2025 and May 2026 is from senior roles

slides.title: I'd still learn to code. {I'd just change what I focus on.}
slides.body: Three or four years ago, most of the focus was syntax and for loops.

slides.title: Read the code AI writes for you
slides.body: AI writes a lot of code now, and a lot of people don't even read it. Reading it is how you tell what it does and if it's what you asked for.

note.say: What if this email already has an account?

slides.title: An AI fix can hide the real problem

ba.label: Before: sign-up fails
ba.t: Error: this email already has an account

ba.label: After the AI's quick fix
ba.t: No error shown. The user still isn't signed up.

slides.body: Debugging is how you know if a fix is for the actual problem.

slides.title: The same payment can reach your server twice
slides.body: Many payment providers send the message again if your server doesn't reply in time. So learn how webhooks and retries work.

slides.title: Know the business your code is for
slides.body: AI can build a stock app for a pharmacy very quickly. It won't always know that the pharmacy has to sell the medicine that expires first.

slides.title: Learn to code, {but don't count on it to hand you a junior role.}
slides.body: If you hire developers: are you still hiring juniors?
